courses.title: C++ Foundations — Levels 1–5
courses.summary: All 52 lessons from the master curriculum: runnable examples, code you write and run, and a quiz per lesson.

courses.title: C++ Intermediate — Levels 6–8
courses.summary: 31 lessons on references, classes and object-oriented programming, translated from the master curriculum.

courses.title: C++ Templates — Levels 9
courses.summary: Templates: one algorithm for many types, from the first function template to C++17 constraints.

courses.title: C++ Advanced — Levels 10–12
courses.summary: 26 lessons on the standard library, move semantics and exceptions. Version 0.1.22 adds the standard exception hierarchy, the three containers the usual tour leaves out (forward_list, unordered_multiset, unordered_multimap), what a container adapter is, and a noexcept that depends on the type.

courses.title: C++ Testing and Structure — Levels 13–15
courses.summary: 24 lessons on testing, streams and files, and splitting a program across headers and sources.

courses.title: C++ Algorithms and Concurrency — Levels 16–18
courses.summary: 26 lessons on data structures, concurrency and performance. Version 0.1.21 adds the doubly linked list and the space cost of its second pointer, std::recursive_mutex, and std::packaged_task.

courses.title: C++ Design and Mastery — Levels 19–20
courses.summary: 16 lessons on designing larger programs and a four-lesson capstone that builds one program end to end.

courses.title: C++ Revision — Language Core and Library Gaps
courses.summary: 28 revision lessons closing the gaps between Levels 9 and 20: type aliases, decltype, value categories, alignment, bit masks, the missing algorithms, variant and any, string_view, the preprocessor, iterator-generic code and testing.

courses.title: C++ Revision — Data Structures, Algorithms and Memory
courses.summary: 25 revision lessons on the structures and algorithms the levels build on: linked lists, stacks and ring buffers, binary search trees, AVL rotations, heaps, tries, graphs, hashing, complexity, recursion, dynamic programming, sorting, allocators, std::pmr, perfect forwarding and a thread pool.

courses.title: C++ Memory Model and Object Lifetime — Levels 21–23
courses.summary: 16 lessons on what the standard actually promises: happens-before and data races, memory orders, undefined behaviour and how to detect it, the five regions of a program, stack frames, static initialisation order, object sizing, construction and destruction, temporaries and storage reuse.

courses.title: C++ Preprocessor, Modules and Namespaces — Levels 24–26
courses.summary: 24 lessons on the preprocessor, modules and namespaces: #include, #define and conditional compilation, header guards, function-like and variadic macros with #, ## and __VA_OPT__, why modules exist, module interfaces, partitions, import and export, the global module fragment, how to compile a module, and every namespace form including anonymous, inline and argument-dependent lookup.

courses.title: C++ Advanced STL, Ranges and Utilities — Levels 27–29
courses.summary: 25 lessons on the containers and library utilities that finish the standard library: vector size and capacity, iterator invalidation, the erase-remove idiom, choosing a container by complexity, map and set, std::array, ranges and views including filter, transform, take, drop, split and pipelines, then variant, optional with monadic chaining, any, string_view, span, std::expected, and std::pmr pool resources with pool_options.

courses.title: C++ Time, Randomness, Regex and Debugging — Levels 30–32
courses.summary: 24 lessons on the parts of C++ that touch the real world: chrono durations, clocks, time points and the C++20 calendar, time zones against fixed offsets, formatting a date, then random engines, distributions instead of modulo and how to seed them, then std::regex from regex_match through capture groups, regex_replace and sregex_iterator, and finally debugging: assert and static_assert, reading a call stack and stepping, breakpoints and watch expressions, hunting leaks and use-after-free, and the sanitizers and debuggers that find them.

courses.title: C++ Build Systems, Linking and Architecture — Levels 33–35
courses.summary: 26 lessons on how a program is made and how it is structured: the four stages behind one compiler command, optimisation levels and build defines, Make, Ninja and CMake, then linking from symbols through static and shared libraries, and finally design principles, the classic patterns and architecture. Version 0.1.24 adds MSBuild's properties, items and targets, and names the Abstract Factory pattern.

courses.title: C++ Testing, Performance and Threads — Levels 36–38
courses.summary: 24 lessons on proving a program works and making it fast: what a test is, unit, integration and system tests, test doubles that replace the clock and the disk, what a test framework does behind its macros, fixtures and fresh state, table-driven boundary tests and how to make code testable at all, then performance engineering by measurement rather than guesswork, optimisation levels, counting calls and counting work, reading a profiler, counting allocations, cache lines and traversal order, data layout, branch prediction, vectorisation and false sharing, and finally threads: the shared-memory rule, locks and the size of a critical section, thread pools and work queues, condition variables, atomics and memory order, lock-free progress guarantees, parallel algorithms and the limits of scaling.

courses.title: C++ Networking, Databases and GUIs — Levels 39–41
courses.summary: 24 lessons on the three levels that take a program outside its own process: networking, databases and graphical interfaces. Networking begins with addresses, ports and byte order, then a TCP server in five calls and a client that talks to it, then UDP and what a stream actually promises, then HTTP as text on the wire and the parsers a framework hides, then names and getaddrinfo, then serving many clients with a thread each and where that stops, then framing a message out of a stream, and finally Asio, gRPC, queues and timeouts. Database programming covers tables and queries, prepared statements and injection, transactions and rollback, the N+1 problem and counted round trips, connection pools that leak, indexes and their write cost, normalisation, and choosing an engine. GUI development covers the event loop and hit testing, signals and slots, layouts computed rather than written, model and view, keeping logic out of widgets, long work and thread affinity, retained versus immediate mode, and the six behaviours a screenshot cannot show.

courses.title: C++ Games, Embedded Systems and Operating Systems — Levels 42-44
courses.summary: Eight lessons on games, eight on embedded C++ and eight on operating systems: fixed-timestep loops, input queues, physics, box collision and response, entities and components; registers, interrupts, deadlines, fixed point, memory maps, schedulers, ring buffers and pools; and system calls, processes, page tables, IPC, files and kernel space. Every card you can run, runs; what needs a window, a chip or kernel privilege is text beside a model that prints the same numbers.

courses.title: C++ Linux, Windows and Security — Levels 45-47
courses.summary: Eight lessons on Linux systems programming, eight on Windows and eight on security. File descriptors, fork and copy-on-write, exec and argv, pipes and the framing they lack, signals and async-signal safety, mmap, processes against threads, and a shell in miniature; then handles, kernel objects and reference counts, the registry, services in session zero, Winsock, the wide-character API and surrogate pairs, COM, and an abstraction over both platforms; then threat modelling, buffer overruns, integer overflow, secure memory that is not optimised away, hashing, constant-time comparison, randomness, and the hardening layers from ASLR to code signing. Every mechanism runs as portable C++; the POSIX and Win32 calls it stands for are shown beside it.

courses.title: C++ Templates, Compilers and the Standard — Levels 48–50
courses.summary: Levels 48 to 50 close the course: advanced templates from instantiation to diagnostics, compiler internals built card by card - lexer, parser, AST, IR, optimisation passes, code generation and the ABI - and the standard itself, from feature-test macros and deprecation to the release train that ends at C++26.

courses.title: C++ Professional Practice, Expert Techniques and Coroutines — Levels 51–53
courses.summary: 24 lessons on the work that separates a programmer who can write C++ from one a team depends on. Level 51 is professional practice: a history a reviewer can read, a CI pipeline that gates rather than decorates, warnings as errors, sanitizers and static analysis. Level 52 is expert technique: pimpl and ABI stability, argument-dependent lookup, hidden friends and customization points, pointer provenance, expression templates, and a small executor. Level 53 is coroutines from the frame outwards: a promise_type written by hand, co_yield, co_return, custom awaitables, counting and removing allocations, lazy pipelines and cancellation.

courses.title: C++ Library Design and Real Projects — Levels 54–55
courses.summary: The last two levels: designing and shipping a C++ library — header-only, static and shared, ABI stability, versioning and packaging — then six real programs built end to end: a calculator, a ring-buffer logger, a thread pool, a binary file format, a command-line tool and a test harness.
